# Block-direct-sum no-gain theorem

**Status:** `PROPOSED NATIVE BARRIER THEOREM / EXACT FINITE ALGEBRA`

This note closes a tempting but empty extension: stacking several already-normalized scalar-window compressions as independent blocks.

## 1. Setup

For `j=1,...,q`, let

```text
R_j=P_j+Q_j
```

be Hermitian compressions of the same zero window, in units where each simple on-line atom has trace at most one. Suppose:

- `P_j>=0` is generated by the same set of `S` simple on-line zeros, so `rank(P_j)<=S`;
- `Q_j` has at most `B` positive directions, one per non-simple/on-line or off-line packet in the relevant count argument;
- each block separately yields a count certificate `L_j` through the rank–trace inequality and the same multiplicity count `N`.

Form the uncoupled block direct sum

```text
R_direct = R_1 direct_sum ... direct_sum R_q.
```

## 2. Theorem for the simple/on-line c=2 certificate

The direct-sum certificate is the arithmetic mean of the block certificates:

```text
L_direct = (1/q) sum_j L_j <= max_j L_j.
```

Hence a block-diagonal ensemble cannot improve on the best constituent scalar window.

### Proof

The positive block satisfies

```text
rank(P_direct)=sum_j rank(P_j)<=qS,
```

and the index bound is

```text
n_+(Q_direct)=sum_j n_+(Q_j)<=qB.
```

Trace and Frobenius square add exactly:

```text
tr(R_direct)=sum_j tr(R_j),
||R_direct||_F^2=sum_j ||R_j||_F^2.
```

Applying the `c=2` rank–trace inequality to the direct sum and then dividing the resulting rank bound by `q` gives exactly the average of the `q` separate right-hand sides. The average is at most their maximum. `square`

## 3. Multiplicity-aware and c=3 versions

The same argument applies to the parameter-`c` multiplicity charge and to the `c=3` distinct-zero certificate because:

- the on-line atom list is repeated once per block;
- positive indices add under direct sum;
- every charge and moment term is additive.

Thus no uncoupled block ensemble improves any linear count bound obtained from the same rank–trace family.

## 4. What the theorem does not rule out

It does not cover a genuinely coupled block matrix

```text
R_mixed = [R_ij]_(1<=i,j<=q)
```

with nonzero mixed-window entries `R_ij`. Such a matrix may change both the zero-side rank geometry and the prime-side Frobenius cost. It requires mixed moment evaluations and a new matrix-valued variational problem.

It also does not rule out:

- additional spectral moments;
- larger Fourier support;
- a different zero-side polynomial inequality;
- nonlinear combinations of independently certified statements;
- a complete-kernel theorem using information not present in scalar traces.

## 5. Research consequence

The support-one scalar profile is already optimized by Montgomery–Taylor. This theorem adds:

```text
optimized scalar window
+ any finite uncoupled direct-sum collection
= still no improvement beyond the best scalar window.
```

Therefore the next window-based experiment should begin with cross-window entries. A project that merely generates many tapers, evaluates each scalar trace pair, and block-diagonalizes the results is provably searching an empty direction.
